title: How often do you still write code by yourself?
author: mediamuesli

comments.author: Ok-Ninja-8165
comments.body: Less than 10%. It's just easier to write most important code by hand than explain it to model. Defined data structures and interfaces give model good starting point to write code.

replies.author: mediamuesli
replies.body: Could you give an example what kind of code you still tell the ai to exactly execute like you wish?

replies.author: Ok-Ninja-8165
replies.body: Something like how exactly data structures should looks like and which interface given system must have. Exactly areas where AI is incapable of making good decisions.

replies.author: mbreaddit
replies.body: Yes but i don´t actually write them anymore in actual code but rather describe them in pseudocode inside the chat itself, which yields faster typing and i don´t have to bother about syntax, but apart from that, agreed.

comments.author: NoName847
comments.body: 200+ hours deep into my unity game , never once looked at the code , so far everything is working exactly how I want it to work

replies.author: mediamuesli
replies.body: Maybe game programming courses in university will turn to something like film school. Not a place to learn but to build networks and find team members you can trust.

comments.author: chonky_totoro
comments.body: anyone not voting for no hand coding is larping. are you telling me you can code better and faster than Opus 5.5? keep dreaming

replies.author: HuWeiliu
replies.body: To be fair in some areas within coding (architecture) 100% I can do better, but since its so fast, you can usually just iterate yourself through the poor code faster than if you did it by hand and got it right the first time. Though there is quite likely a happy middleground.

replies.author: Comprehensive_Head82
replies.body: Is it actually so hard to believe that there are people that don't use AI at all to code and do everything themselves?

replies.author: Ok-Ninja-8165
replies.body: Not faster but far better. At least I have good idea where all of that is going to move and what I'll need in the future. AI code is just good enough considering how fast it can be generated.

comments.author: crackedpotstudio
comments.body:
Background as hosting engineer with a lot of PHP and MySQL experience, I never ever touch any code at all since that last 2 years. There is a reason I stopped developing tools and websites and Claude is re-igniting that passion without having me go through stackoverflow and countless tutorials all the time.

  
I only wrote the ''tree growing simulator'' part of my bonsai game in HTML to play and tinker with settings, when I was done I let claude translate it on his own to Godot.

comments.author: Dicethrower
comments.body: I'm a gamedev with +15y of experience. I haven't touched an IDE in months now. I stopped staring at the code all together a few weeks ago when the rest of my team finally caught on that we're no longer writing human code for humans. Instead our "programming" language is design docs with rules/intend on how the game should work instead. After that, with the right setup, you rely on claude to do its thing, and it simply does it better than any human would. Especially my latest game is going to be completely vibecoded. It's no longer a "soon" for me, we've been there since September 22. It's just taking people time to figure it out.
